title: Gulf Air 072
summary: Gulf Air Flight 072, an Airbus A320-212 flying from Cairo to Bahrain, crashed into the shallow waters of the Persian Gulf 2 km from the airport on 23 August 2000, minutes after a go-around from a failed approach to Runway 12. The captain suffered spatial disorientation, applying a large nose-down input that produced a 15-degree dive; as the aircraft descended, the crew disregarded the GPWS 'sink rate' and 'Whoop, whoop, pull up' warnings while debating flap configuration instead. The Airbus struck the sea at 280 knots, killing all 143 people on board.
probable_cause: The final report found non-adherence to Standard Operating Procedures and loss of spatial and situational awareness by the crew during the approach and go-around, compounded by deficient CRM training at Gulf Air and safety oversight failures by the civil aviation authority.

factors.evidence: The flight crew suffered from spatial disorientation during the go-around and crashed into the shallow waters of the Persian Gulf.
Non-adherence to a number of Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) by the aircraft crew during the approach and final phases of the flight.
Systemic factors also contributed to the accident, including deficiency in crew resource management (CRM) training by Gulf Air.
Instead of responding to the sink rate warning, the captain ordered flap retraction as the GPWS escalated to 'Whoop, whoop! Pull up!'
Safety oversights by the Directorate General Of Civil Aviation and Meteorology of Oman.
Flying with a speed of 280 knots and a nose-down pitch of 6.5 degrees, the aircraft slammed onto the sea below, instantly killing all 143 passengers and crew members.

events.text: Captain Shakeeb applied a large nose-down input, inducing a rapid descent at a pitch angle of approximately 15 degrees, the maximum permissible, as the aircraft continued to accelerate under TO/GA thrust.
As the first officer called 'flaps three,' the Ground Proximity Warning System issued a 'sink rate' alert, but instead of responding to the warning, the captain ordered flap retraction.
As the aircraft descended toward the sea, the GPWS escalated to 'Whoop, whoop! Pull up!' while the crew continued discussing flap position as the aircraft descended unchecked.
At 19:30, flying at 280 knots with a nose-down pitch of 6.5 degrees, the aircraft slammed onto the sea, instantly killing all 143 passengers and crew members.
